Launch-recoverable bootstrap needs explicit authenticated reissue/revoke+next-generation operation, or an independently reviewed existing-key encrypted delivery design; neither may be fabricated from native receipt. Do not mark retry flow complete from create-only happy path.

Reissue must be closed own manage_identity/environment operation, expected device version, org/device serialization, atomically revoke current enrollment then issue next exact native generation; preserve original exact token/enroll replay. No credential rotation shortcut, no revocation of unrelated credentials as implicit repair.

Gateway enroll request must be durably persisted with original credential_id, keypair/publickey, generation, keyID and EXACT chosen expiry before retry. Generating a new expiry/id/key on retry changes native enrollment digest and conflicts; do not coerce native replay.

An expired or revoked one-time token cannot authenticate even for old enrollment replay; consumed alone is not revocation. Returned credential receipt replay must still be checked against CURRENT credential authority and real clock, so revoked/rotated old credential never becomes usable.

Native receipt omits full scope/publickey. HTTP/bootstrap response must bind actual derived scope/device/key/generation using current native authority and expected client publickey, not just result id or a fabricated response mapping.
